release_change_policy: Treat every different IOS image as a separate validation target; inspect exact startup script, kernel/driver, VF mapping and allocation policy, then adapt only a separately named guarded candidate if needed. Do not disable existing guards to force another image.

Activation/reboot loses the current RAM correction even when the retained USB script is unchanged. A target may fix the allocation logic itself, retain the mismatch or change it; none is established without examination.
Archived17.18.3a/26.1.1 and current uncorrected26.2.1 show related allocation failures; a simple downgrade is not an established fix.

Keep IOS-image changes separate from ROMMON/boot-firmware changes. Production compatibility recommendations do not establish prototype compatibility; A already demonstrates pre-ROMMON TPM halt after release ROMMON programming.

Before downgrade, inspect/back up IOx/application data. Cisco26.2.1 notes document loss of the6GB IOx persistent disk contents if an earlier image replaces it with4GB. Applicability to actual installed apps must be checked; no such cleanup/downgrade performed.
